# @rxova/react-rating-input

> A headless, accessible rating input for React. Any icon, any precision — whole,
> half or continuous fills. Interactive it is a real `radiogroup` of real radios,
> so keyboard, focus, form submission and screen-reader announcements come from
> the browser; read-only it is an image with a label. Zero runtime dependencies.
> No stylesheet to import.

## Install

    npm install @rxova/react-rating-input

`react >= 18` is the only peer dependency.

## Minimal working example

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { Rating } from '@rxova/react-rating-input'

export function Feedback() {
  const [score, setScore] = useState(0)

  return <Rating value={score} onChange={setScore} precision={0.5} label="Rate your meal" />
}
```

Passing `onChange` is what makes it interactive. Without it the component renders
a read-only score, and that is the intended way to show one.

## Props

`<Rating>` — the full surface is `RatingProps` in the published types.

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `number` | — | Controlled score. Clamped to `[0, max]`; NaN/Infinity become 0. |
| `defaultValue` | `number` | — | Uncontrolled initial score. Ignored when `value` is set. |
| `max` | `number` | `5` | Number of icons. Positive integer. |
| `precision` | `number` | `0` | Quantization grid: `1` whole, `0.5` halves, `0` continuous. |
| `rounding` | `'nearest' \| 'down' \| 'up' \| 'none'` | `'nearest'` | Direction of the snap onto the grid. |
| `icon` | `ReactNode \| ((state: RatingIconState) => ReactNode)` | a built-in star | A function receives per-icon state. |
| `emptyIcon` | `ReactNode \| ((state: RatingIconState) => ReactNode)` | same as `icon`, dimmed | Track icon. |
| `onChange` | `(value: number) => void` | — | **Providing this is what makes the component interactive.** |
| `onHoverChange` | `(value: number \| null) => void` | — | Hover/keyboard preview; `null` when the preview ends. |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` | `!onChange` | Force read-only even with `onChange` present. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | |
| `allowClear` | `boolean` | `true` when interactive | Re-selecting the current value clears to 0. |
| `name` | `string` | — | Radio group name; also emits a value a native `<form>` can read. |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | Sets `aria-invalid` and `data-invalid` on the group. |
| `onBlur` | `(event: FocusEvent<HTMLElement>) => void` | — | Fires when focus leaves the group, not when moving between icons. |
| `label` | `string` | — | Accessible name for the group. |
| `formatLabel` | `(value: number, max: number) => string` | `` `${value} out of ${max}` `` | Formats the default accessible name. |
| `formatOptionLabel` | `(value: number, max: number) => string` | — | Accessible name for one option. |
| `aria-describedby` | `string` | — | ids of external error/help text. |
| `id` | `string` | — | Base id; options derive `${id}-1`, `${id}-2`, … |
| `dir` | `'ltr' \| 'rtl'` | inherited | Flips the fill origin. |
| `className` | `string` | — | |
| `style` | `CSSProperties` | — | |
| `onWarn` | `(warning: RatingWarning) => void` | `console.warn` | Development-only notice that a prop was coerced. Stripped from production builds. |

Also exported: the `useRating` hook, for building your own markup.

## Warnings

An out-of-range prop never throws. The component coerces it into something it
can paint and reports what it did through `onWarn`, which receives a
`RatingWarning`: `{ code, prop, received, used, message }` — the value as
received, the value actually used after coercion, and a message safe to log.

`RatingWarningCode` is one of `value-non-finite`, `value-negative`,
`value-above-max`, `max-non-finite`, `max-too-small`, `max-non-integer`.

    <Rating value={7} max={5} onWarn={(w) => log(w.message)} />
    // { code: 'value-above-max', prop: 'value', received: 7, used: 5, … }

This is a development signal — usually a value arriving from an API in an
unexpected range — and is stripped from production builds.

## Styling

There is no stylesheet. Set CSS custom properties on any ancestor:

`--rx-rating-size`, `--rx-rating-gap`, `--rx-rating-color-filled`, `--rx-rating-color-empty`,
`--rx-rating-color-hover`, `--rx-rating-empty-filter`, `--rx-rating-focus-ring`,
`--rx-rating-focus-ring-offset`, `--rx-rating-focus-ring-radius`, `--rx-rating-transition`.

Or target the `data-*` attributes, which are public API covered by semver:
`data-rx-rating-root`, `data-rx-rating-item`, `data-rx-rating-layer`, plus the state hooks
`data-state`, `data-fill`, `data-active`, `data-disabled`, `data-readonly`,
`data-invalid`, `data-idx`.

## Three mistakes to avoid

1. **Adding `readOnly` to get a display-only score.** Omitting `onChange` already
   does that, and it is the better route: the component then renders as an image
   with a label rather than as a disabled form control, which is what a screen
   reader should hear for a score that is being reported rather than collected.
2. **Importing a stylesheet.** There is none. Colour and size are CSS custom
   properties — a `Rating` that renders invisible is almost always
   `--rx-rating-color-filled` inheriting a background-coloured value, not a bug.
3. **Assuming `precision` rounds the value you pass in.** `precision` is the grid
   the *user's* input snaps to. A `value` you supply is displayed as given, at
   whatever fractional fill it implies — that is what makes a 3.7-star average
   render honestly.
